Para1:
"Large language model inference on a single GPU is often governed less by raw floating point throughput than by the movement of tensors between high bandwidth memory and the processor. During autoregressive decoding, each generated token requires a forward pass that reads the model weights and the key value cache for every previous token, while producing only one new token. The arithmetic intensity of this step is low, especially for small batch sizes, so the GPU spends a large fraction of its time waiting for memory. This observation motivates a family of systems techniques that reduce the number of expensive memory accesses per accepted token, improve the locality of attention computation, and manage the key value cache so that it does not become the dominant traffic source. Speculative decoding, flash attention, and key value cache traffic control are three such techniques, and they interact in subtle ways when deployed on a single accelerator."
